claims.claim: The Martyrdom of Polycarp is written as an encyclical letter from the church of God at Smyrna to the church of God at Philomelium (in Phrygia) and to all congregations of the holy and catholic church in every place.
Its stated purpose is to give an account of the martyrs, especially the blessed Polycarp, who ended the persecution and, as it were, set a seal on it by his martyrdom.
Polycarp was bishop of Smyrna (modern İzmir, Turkey), and the Martyrdom of Polycarp is the earliest account of Christian martyrdom outside the New Testament.
The Ante-Nicene Christian Library introduction calls it the earliest of all the Martyria and generally the most interesting and authentic.
The date of composition is disputed: it has commonly been placed in the middle of the second century, but some scholars think the text interpolated in places and some assign it a much later date.
A database entry dates the Greek text to Smyrna between the late 2nd and 3rd centuries and says interpolations in the 3rd or 4th century are possible.
